text:
zoe: hitting a weird edge case during an onboarding call. Our SDK's public generic overloads collapse to `any` when consumed via an ESM import after the app is bundled for Edge. Repro attached: https://github.com/redwood/repro-edge-exports-ts 

harry: ouch. smallest repro?

zoe: minimal SDK surface: 
```ts
// packages/sdk/src/index.ts
export function rpc<T>(payload: T): Promise<{ data: T }>;
export function rpc(payload: unknown) { return Promise.resolve({ data: payload as any }); }
```
consumer:
```ts
import { rpc } from '@redwood/sdk';

type Req = { uid: string };
async function test(){
  const res = await rpc<Req>({ uid: 'u' });
  // expect res.data -> Req. in Edge ESM bundle it becomes `any` (no intellisense)
}
```

zoe: two important details: our package.json exports map has an `import` entry that points at `dist/esm/index.js`, and our build writes a tiny wrapper `dist/esm/index.js` that only re-exports `./lib`. We run `tsc --emitDeclarationOnly` against source but then run a dts bundler for the esm artifact which appears to flatten overloads.

kevin: flattening from dts bundler rings a bell. Which tool are you using to bundle d.ts? api-extractor or dts-bundle-generator? They have known overload edge-cases.

zoe: we use `rollup-plugin-dts` as a post-step for esm. The cjs package keeps raw `.d.ts` files and preserves overloads; the esm bundle output is a single `index.d.ts` produced by rollup-plugin-dts and it shows the widened signature (payload: any).

maria: two action items: 1) stop shipping a bundler-generated d.ts that loses overloads, 2) ensure `types` in package.json points to a stable d.ts that preserves overloads. Also consider `typesVersions` to guide TS in edge cases.

harry: quick workaround for users: deep-import the cjs entry: `import { rpc } from '@redwood/sdk/dist/cjs'` or pin to a release before we started bundling d.ts. Not great UX but helps.

kevin: long-term fix options: a) switch to api-extractor with proper tsdoc and rollup output (config must preserve overloads), b) generate explicit public index.d.ts by hand for the most common APIs, or c) avoid bundling types at all and point `exports.import` to the compiled ESM file that already has its d.ts emitted alongside it.

zoe: I also noticed `moduleResolution: "bundler"` in many consumer tsconfigs (Vercel/Esm setups); that makes TS resolve to the esm export path which picks the bundler-generated d.ts. If we want to be defensive, we should make sure that the esm export's d.ts is correct.

maria: add a CI smoke test: publish a local tarball, install into a tiny Edge fixture that uses `moduleResolution: bundler`, run `npx tsc --noEmit` and fail on missing completions. Also add a declaration-emit diff between cjs and esm artifacts to detect API shrinkage.

packager-bot: Created ticket RW-DX-9001: "ESM d.ts bundling flattens overloads and widens generics for Edge consumers" (attached repro).

kevin: i'll pick this up. Plan: 1) reproduce locally with the repro app, 2) try replacing rollup-plugin-dts with api-extractor or emitting parallel d.ts and avoid bundling, 3) add CI check that diffs public declarations between package entries, 4) doc short-term workaround in SDK README.

harry: FYI one more gotcha: we had `types` pointing at `dist/types/index.d.ts` while `exports.import` pointed at `dist/esm/index.js`. TS will resolve to the `.d.ts` next to the resolved entry, so the bundler-generated `dist/esm/index.d.ts` was winning even though `dist/types/index.d.ts` had the correct overloads. Aligning `types` with `exports` fixed local repro for me.

zoe: good tip. i'll add that alignment as a checklist item in our publish docs. I'll attach a minimal script that compares `index.d.ts` files in the packed tarball.

maria: also add a tiny test that asserts that exported API surfaces are structurally identical (use `ts-api-guardian` or `api-extractor` report compare). That will stop accidental regressions.

kevin: PR incoming. thanks for the clear repro and notes. :thumbsup:
